newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Japan Air System aims for Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Japan Air System aims for Hong Kong.

text.p: Japan Air System has made the first move to start a new service between Osaka's Kansai airport and Hong Kong, a spokesman for the territory's Civil Aviation Department told Reuters.
The spokesman said JAS has applied for slot allocations at Kai Tak airport from June which is the prelude to a formal application for a certificate of operation.

Aviation sources said with Kai Tak notoriously congested and the Civil Aviation Department turning down around 150 applications a week for additional air services, approval for the JAS newcomer is far from certain.

The sources said the Tokyo-based regional and domestic scheduled and charter airline has also applied to Japan's Transport Ministry for the four times a week service using one of the airline's 14 Airbus A300-600R aircraft.

The application is being seen as a sign of increasing competition on the route. Hong Kong's de facto flag carrier Cathay Pacific, which said Japan is its most profitable market for both passengers and cargo started four new afternoon flights a week from Hong Kong to Osaka earlier this month.

Japan's All Nippon Airways also plans to increase capacity between Hong Kong and Kansai when it replaces Boeing 767s with new Boeing 777 aircraft later this year. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
